solutions.title: Two Sum
solutions.approach: Use a hash map to store each number and its index as I iterate through the array. For each number, calculate the complement needed to reach the target. If that complement is already in the map, return the two indices; otherwise, store the current number and continue.

solutions.title: Add Two Numbers
solutions.approach: Traverse both linked lists together, add the corresponding digits plus any carry, and build a new linked list with the result digits until both lists and the carry are exhausted.

solutions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
solutions.approach: Use a sliding window and a set to track characters in the current substring. Expand the right side of the window, and when a duplicate appears, move the left side forward while removing characters until the substring is unique again. Track the maximum window length.

solutions.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
solutions.approach: Use binary search on the smaller sorted array to find a partition where all values on the left side are less than or equal to all values on the right side. Once the correct partition is found, compute the median from the boundary values without merging the arrays.

solutions.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
solutions.approach: Expand outward from every possible center, checking both odd- and even-length palindromes. Track the starting index and length of the longest palindrome found, then return that substring.

solutions.title: zigzag conversion
solutions.approach: Simulate the zigzag by placing each character into its current row while moving down and then back up. Reverse direction at the first and last rows, then concatenate all rows.

solutions.title: Reverse Integer
solutions.approach: I get the last digit one at a time and append it to the reverslse. Before I multiply by 10 and adding the next digit, I check whether that would exceed the 32 bit integer range, and return 0 if it does.
